findings.finding: The plan asserts the new mutation-gate job 'participates in Gerrit Verified' and runs scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py, but does not enumerate the concrete consumer edits that parity gate requires: adding the blocking job to vote.needs in .github/workflows/gerrit-verify.yaml AND to a source mirror lane (or updating SOURCE_WORKFLOWS/EXCLUDED_JOBS in check_verify_gate_parity.py). Without these edits, check_verify_gate_parity.py will fail the build.
findings.location: Design (Gerrit patchset) + Acceptance Criteria line 'The job participates in Gerrit Verified' + Verification (python scripts/check_verify_gate_parity.py)
scenarios: The mutation Validate job is added as a blocking gate but is not listed in vote.needs and not in a SOURCE_WORKFLOWS mirror lane — the plan's own Verification step (check_verify_gate_parity.py) or the green-verify/red-main hole recurs.
findings.suggested_fix: In Design, add a bullet naming the wiring: the blocking mutation-gate job is added to gerrit-verify.yaml vote.needs and appears in one of the SOURCE_WORKFLOWS mirror lanes (test.yml/optionality.yml/etc.); the weekly/manual all-shard workflow, being workflow_dispatch/schedule-only, is either kept out of SOURCE_WORKFLOWS or justified in EXCLUDED_JOBS.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State how a patch that changes both mapped source and a test/support input in the same shard is classified, and whether any strict transition evidence is retained for the unchanged-mutant subset in that case.
evidence: 'For a test/support-only change, production bytes and mutant identities are stable.'
'For a source-changing patch, exact mutant IDs and killed counts are advisory because valid edits can add, delete, or renumber mutants.'

ABSENCE: neither section states how a patch touching both source and tests in one shard is classified; the strict transition check is the plan's 'direct evidence that a changed test weakened behavior' and it is silently dropped for such mixed patches.
findings.finding: The design's two comparison modes (strict mutant-ID transition for test/support-only changes vs advisory-IDs-plus-budgets for source-changing patches) do not state how a MIXED patch that changes both a mapped source file AND a test/support input in the same shard is classified. Under the plain reading it falls into the source-changing branch, which disables the direct killed-to-non-killed transition check and leans only on the survivor/score budgets — allowing an author to weaken a test while making any trivial source edit in the same shard to escape the strict comparison.
scenarios: A patch edits src/rebar/signing.py trivially and simultaneously guts an assertion in tests/unit/test_signing.py; classified as source-changing, so the killed-to-non-killed check is skipped and only budgets guard the shard.
A shard with a non-zero survivor ceiling (e.g. next batch: 6) could absorb a newly-uncaught mutant within the ceiling on a mixed patch.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to 'Comparison and budgets' specifying mixed patches: e.g. classify per input so unchanged production mutant identities still get the strict killed-to-non-killed check, and only genuinely renumbered/added mutants fall back to advisory-plus-budget treatment — or explicitly justify that the survivor/score budgets are the accepted backstop for mixed shards.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare which artifact is the single source of truth for the shard mapping/budgets/fingerprints (manifest vs pyproject [tool.mutmut] vs docs/mutation-testing.md), and derive or bidirectionally validate the others from it rather than maintaining three parallel copies.

Plan: 'Validation proves every current only_mutate and selected-test entry is represented' — acknowledges the overlap but establishes cross-check, not single-source derivation
findings.finding: The proposed shard manifest re-encodes shard mapping data that already lives in two places: pyproject.toml [tool.mutmut] (only_mutate list and pytest_add_cli_args_test_selection) and docs/mutation-testing.md (per-module test mapping table, numeric budgets, and the equivalent-mutant fingerprints). The plan adds a third representation and only guarantees a validation cross-check, not a single source of truth.
findings.location: Design, first bullet ('Add one machine-readable shard manifest')
scenarios: An author widens only_mutate in pyproject.toml but forgets the manifest, or updates a budget in docs but not the manifest — three artifacts must be kept mutually consistent
